subject: Physics
question_text: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 2 m/s^2. How far does it travel in the first 5 s, and what is its speed at that instant?
hint: Starting from rest means u = 0. Pick the equation that contains s, a and t but not v.

subject: Physics
question_text: A ball is projected at 20 m/s at 30 degrees above the horizontal (g = 10 m/s^2). Find the time of flight and the maximum height.
solution_steps: Step 1: Vertical component u sin(theta) = 20 x 0.5 = 10 m/s. Step 2: T = 2u sin(theta)/g = 2(10)/10 = 2 s. Step 3: H = (u sin(theta))^2/(2g) = 100/20 = 5 m.
hint: Only the vertical component of the velocity decides the time of flight and height. Resolve it first.

subject: Physics
question_text: A boat can move at 5 m/s in still water. A river 100 m wide flows at 3 m/s. What is the minimum crossing time, and how far downstream does the boat drift in that case?
solution_steps: Step 1: Minimum time needs the boat to head perpendicular to the bank. Step 2: t = width / v_boat = 100/5 = 20 s. Step 3: Drift = v_river x t = 3 x 20 = 60 m.
hint: River flow does not change the crossing time when you head straight across. Time depends only on the perpendicular speed.

subject: Physics
question_text: A stone is thrown vertically upward at 20 m/s (g = 10 m/s^2). Find the maximum height and the total time before it returns to the thrower's hand.
solution_steps: Step 1: At the top v = 0, so H = u^2/(2g) = 400/20 = 20 m. Step 2: Time to rise = u/g = 2 s. Step 3: Total time = 2 x 2 = 4 s.
hint: At the highest point the velocity is zero. Use v^2 = u^2 - 2gH, and double the rise time for the total.

subject: Physics
question_text: A car covers the first half of a journey at 40 km/h and the second half at 60 km/h. Find its average speed for the whole journey.
solution_steps: Step 1: Equal distances, so use the harmonic mean. Step 2: v_avg = 2 x 40 x 60/(40 + 60) = 4800/100 = 48 km/h.
hint: The times are different for the two halves, so the simple mean of 40 and 60 is wrong. Use total distance over total time.

subject: Physics
question_text: A body starts from rest with a uniform acceleration of 4 m/s^2. Find the distance it covers in the 5th second.
solution_steps: Step 1: s_n = u + a(2n - 1)/2 with u = 0, a = 4, n = 5. Step 2: s_5 = 4 x 9/2 = 18 m.
hint: The 5th second is the interval from t = 4 s to t = 5 s, not the first 5 seconds.

subject: Physics
question_text: A ball rolls off a table 1.25 m high with a horizontal speed of 4 m/s (g = 10 m/s^2). Find the time to reach the floor and the horizontal distance covered.
solution_steps: Step 1: Vertical motion from rest: h = (1/2)g t^2, so t = sqrt(2 x 1.25/10) = sqrt(0.25) = 0.5 s. Step 2: Horizontal distance = 4 x 0.5 = 2 m.
hint: The horizontal speed does not affect the fall time. Find the time from the vertical motion alone.

subject: Physics
question_text: A car moving at 30 m/s brakes uniformly and stops in 5 s. Find the deceleration and the stopping distance.
hint: The final velocity is zero. Use v = u + at first, then v^2 = u^2 + 2as.

subject: Physics
question_text: A ball is thrown at 45 degrees and lands on level ground 40 m away (g = 10 m/s^2). Find its speed of projection.
solution_steps: Step 1: R = u^2 sin(2 theta)/g. Step 2: sin 90 = 1, so 40 = u^2/10 and u^2 = 400. Step 3: u = 20 m/s.
hint: For a level-ground projectile use the range formula. At 45 degrees sin(2 theta) = 1.

subject: Physics
question_text: A velocity-time graph rises uniformly from 0 to 10 m/s in 4 s, stays constant for 6 s, then falls uniformly to 0 in 2 s. Find the total displacement and the average velocity.
solution_steps: Step 1: Area of the first triangle = (1/2)(4)(10) = 20 m. Step 2: Rectangle = 6 x 10 = 60 m. Step 3: Last triangle = (1/2)(2)(10) = 10 m. Step 4: Total = 90 m over 12 s, so v_avg = 7.5 m/s.
hint: Displacement is the total area under the v-t graph. Split it into a triangle, a rectangle and a triangle.

subject: Physics
question_text: A 5 kg block on a smooth horizontal surface is pulled by a 20 N force. Find its acceleration and its speed after 3 s from rest.
solution_steps: Step 1: F = ma gives a = 20/5 = 4 m/s^2. Step 2: v = u + at = 0 + 4 x 3 = 12 m/s.
hint: On a smooth surface the net force is just the applied force. Divide it by the mass.

subject: Physics
question_text: A block slides down a rough incline of angle 37 degrees (sin = 0.6, cos = 0.8) with coefficient of kinetic friction 0.25. Find its acceleration (g = 10 m/s^2).
solution_steps: Step 1: Along the slope mg sin(theta) - mu N = ma, with N = mg cos(theta). Step 2: a = g(sin(theta) - mu cos(theta)) = 10(0.6 - 0.25 x 0.8). Step 3: a = 10(0.6 - 0.2) = 4 m/s^2 down the slope.
hint: Resolve the weight along and perpendicular to the slope. Friction uses the perpendicular component (the normal force), not mg.

subject: Physics
question_text: Masses of 4 kg and 2 kg hang on either side of a light frictionless pulley (Atwood machine, g = 10 m/s^2). Find the acceleration and the string tension.
solution_steps: Step 1: The heavier mass goes down: 4g - T = 4a and T - 2g = 2a. Step 2: Add the two equations: 2g = 6a, so a = 20/6 = 3.33 m/s^2. Step 3: T = 2(g + a) = 2(13.33) = 26.7 N.
hint: Write one equation per mass with the same acceleration magnitude, then add them to eliminate T.

subject: Physics
question_text: A 0.5 kg ball moving at 10 m/s is brought to rest by a wall in 0.1 s. Find the average force on the ball.
solution_steps: Step 1: Impulse = change in momentum = 0.5 x 10 = 5 N s. Step 2: F = J/t = 5/0.1 = 50 N.
hint: Impulse equals the change in momentum, and the average force is impulse divided by time.

subject: Physics
question_text: Forces of 30 N towards the east and 40 N towards the north act together on a 5 kg body. Find the magnitude of its acceleration.
solution_steps: Step 1: The forces are perpendicular, so F_net = sqrt(30^2 + 40^2) = 50 N. Step 2: a = F/m = 50/5 = 10 m/s^2.
hint: Add the forces as vectors. For perpendicular forces use Pythagoras.

subject: Physics
question_text: A 0.2 kg stone tied to a 0.5 m string is whirled in a horizontal circle at 5 m/s. Find the tension in the string.
solution_steps: Step 1: The tension supplies the centripetal force. Step 2: T = m v^2/r = 0.2 x 25/0.5 = 10 N.
hint: The tension is the only force towards the centre, so it equals m v^2/r.

subject: Physics
question_text: A 60 kg person stands on a weighing scale in a lift accelerating upward at 2 m/s^2 (g = 10 m/s^2). What does the scale read in newtons?
solution_steps: Step 1: N - mg = ma. Step 2: N = m(g + a) = 60 x 12 = 720 N.
hint: The scale reads the normal force. For an upward acceleration it is larger than the weight.

subject: Physics
question_text: A block just starts to slide on a rough plane when the plane is tilted to a certain angle. If mu_s = 0.577 (that is 1/sqrt(3)), find the angle of repose.
solution_steps: Step 1: At the point of sliding mg sin(theta) = mu_s mg cos(theta). Step 2: tan(theta) = mu_s = 0.577. Step 3: theta = 30 degrees.
hint: At the angle of repose the pull along the slope just equals the limiting friction.

subject: Physics
question_text: A bucket of water is whirled in a vertical circle of radius 0.9 m. Find the minimum speed at the top so that the water does not spill (g = 10 m/s^2).
solution_steps: Step 1: At the top gravity alone can provide the centripetal force at the limit: mg = m v^2/r. Step 2: v = sqrt(g r) = sqrt(10 x 0.9) = sqrt(9) = 3 m/s.
hint: At the minimum speed the normal force from the bucket is zero, so only mg points to the centre.

subject: Physics
question_text: A 3 kg block and a 2 kg block lie on a smooth table joined by a light string. A horizontal 10 N force pulls the 3 kg block away from the 2 kg block. Find the acceleration and the tension.
solution_steps: Step 1: Treat both as one system: a = 10/(3 + 2) = 2 m/s^2. Step 2: The tension alone accelerates the 2 kg block: T = 2 x 2 = 4 N.
hint: Find the common acceleration from the whole system, then apply F = ma to the block that only feels the tension.

subject: Physics
question_text: A force of 10 N pushes a box 5 m along the floor at 60 degrees to the horizontal. Find the work done by the force.
solution_steps: Step 1: W = F d cos(theta). Step 2: W = 10 x 5 x cos 60 = 10 x 5 x 0.5 = 25 J.
hint: Only the component of the force along the displacement does work.

subject: Physics
question_text: A 2 kg ball is dropped from a height of 20 m (g = 10 m/s^2). Using energy conservation find its speed just before it hits the ground.
solution_steps: Step 1: Loss in PE = gain in KE: mgh = (1/2)m v^2. Step 2: v = sqrt(2gh) = sqrt(2 x 10 x 20) = sqrt(400) = 20 m/s.
hint: The mass cancels on both sides, so the speed does not depend on the 2 kg.

subject: Physics
question_text: A 2 kg block moving at 6 m/s collides head-on with a 4 kg block at rest and sticks to it. Find the common speed and the kinetic energy lost.
solution_steps: Step 1: Momentum is conserved: 2 x 6 = (2 + 4) v, so v = 2 m/s. Step 2: Initial KE = (1/2)(2)(36) = 36 J. Step 3: Final KE = (1/2)(6)(4) = 12 J, so the loss is 36 - 12 = 24 J.
hint: Momentum is conserved even when energy is not. Use it for the final speed, then compare the kinetic energies.

subject: Physics
question_text: A motor lifts a 100 kg load through 10 m in 20 s (g = 10 m/s^2). Find the power delivered to the load.
hint: Power is the work done divided by the time taken. The work is the gain in potential energy.

subject: Physics
question_text: A constant force of 20 N moves a body 4 m in the direction of the force. Find the work done and the work done if the force acts at right angles to the motion.
solution_steps: Step 1: W = F d cos(0) = 20 x 4 = 80 J. Step 2: For a perpendicular force cos 90 = 0, so W = 0.
hint: Work depends on the component of the force along the displacement.

subject: Physics
question_text: A spring of force constant 200 N/m is compressed by 0.1 m. Find the energy stored in it.
hint: Spring energy is half k times the square of the compression.

subject: Physics
question_text: Two bodies of masses 1 kg and 4 kg have the same linear momentum. Find the ratio of their kinetic energies.
solution_steps: Step 1: KE = p^2/(2m), so for equal p, KE is proportional to 1/m. Step 2: KE1 : KE2 = m2 : m1 = 4 : 1.
hint: Write the kinetic energy in terms of momentum and mass, not speed.

subject: Physics
question_text: A 1 kg block slides from rest down a smooth incline whose top is 5 m above the bottom (g = 10 m/s^2). Find its speed at the bottom.
solution_steps: Step 1: The surface is smooth so mechanical energy is conserved: mgh = (1/2)m v^2. Step 2: v = sqrt(2gh) = sqrt(100) = 10 m/s.
hint: Only the height matters for a smooth incline, not its angle or length.

subject: Physics
question_text: A ball dropped from 5 m rebounds to 3.2 m after hitting the floor. Find the coefficient of restitution.
solution_steps: Step 1: Speed before impact v1 = sqrt(2 g h1) and after impact v2 = sqrt(2 g h2). Step 2: e = v2/v1 = sqrt(h2/h1) = sqrt(3.2/5) = sqrt(0.64) = 0.8.
hint: Restitution is the ratio of speeds after and before the collision, and speeds come from the heights.

subject: Physics
question_text: A 2 kg block moving at 10 m/s on a rough horizontal surface stops after 20 m (g = 10 m/s^2). Find the friction force and the coefficient of friction.
solution_steps: Step 1: Work-energy theorem: -f x 20 = 0 - (1/2)(2)(100) = -100 J, so f = 5 N. Step 2: mu = f/(mg) = 5/20 = 0.25.
hint: The work done by friction equals the loss in kinetic energy. Then divide by the normal force mg.

subject: Physics
question_text: A uniform solid disc of mass 2 kg and radius 0.5 m is acted on by a torque of 1 N m about its axis. Find its angular acceleration.
hint: First find the moment of inertia of a solid disc about its axis, then use torque = I alpha.

subject: Physics
question_text: A skater spinning at 2 rad/s with moment of inertia 6 kg m^2 pulls in her arms so that her moment of inertia becomes 2 kg m^2. Find her new angular speed.
solution_steps: Step 1: No external torque, so I1 omega1 = I2 omega2. Step 2: 6 x 2 = 2 x omega2. Step 3: omega2 = 6 rad/s.
hint: There is no external torque, so the product I x omega stays the same.

subject: Physics
question_text: A solid sphere rolls without slipping down an incline of 30 degrees. Find its acceleration (g = 10 m/s^2).
solution_steps: Step 1: For a solid sphere I = (2/5)mR^2, so 1 + I/(mR^2) = 1.4. Step 2: a = g sin(theta)/1.4 = 10 x 0.5 / 1.4. Step 3: a = 3.57 m/s^2.
hint: Rolling adds rotational energy, so the acceleration is less than g sin(theta). Use I = (2/5)mR^2.

subject: Physics
question_text: A wheel starts from rest with a constant angular acceleration of 2 rad/s^2. Find its angular velocity and the angle turned after 5 s.
solution_steps: Step 1: omega = omega0 + alpha t = 0 + 2 x 5 = 10 rad/s. Step 2: theta = (1/2) alpha t^2 = 0.5 x 2 x 25 = 25 rad.
hint: The equations are the same as linear motion, with omega, alpha and theta in place of v, a and s.

subject: Physics
question_text: A 2 kg mass is at x = 0 and a 3 kg mass is at x = 5 m. Find the position of their centre of mass.
solution_steps: Step 1: x_cm = (m1 x1 + m2 x2)/(m1 + m2). Step 2: x_cm = (2 x 0 + 3 x 5)/5 = 3 m.
hint: The centre of mass is the mass-weighted average of the positions.

subject: Physics
question_text: A force of 10 N acts perpendicular to a spanner at 0.4 m from the axis of a wheel whose moment of inertia is 2 kg m^2. Find the torque and the angular acceleration.
solution_steps: Step 1: tau = r F = 0.4 x 10 = 4 N m. Step 2: alpha = tau/I = 4/2 = 2 rad/s^2.
hint: When the force is perpendicular to the arm, torque is simply r times F.

subject: Physics
question_text: A uniform disc of mass 2 kg and radius 0.5 m spins at 10 rad/s about its axis. Find its rotational kinetic energy.
hint: Use the disc formula for I first, then half I omega squared.

subject: Physics
question_text: A skater spinning at 2 rad/s with moment of inertia 4 kg m^2 pulls in her arms and her moment of inertia becomes 2 kg m^2. Find her new angular speed.
solution_steps: Step 1: No external torque, so I1 omega1 = I2 omega2. Step 2: omega2 = 4 x 2/2 = 4 rad/s.
hint: Angular momentum is conserved when no external torque acts.

subject: Physics
question_text: A solid sphere rolls without slipping down a 30 degree incline (g = 10 m/s^2). Find the acceleration of its centre.
solution_steps: Step 1: a = g sin(theta)/(1 + 2/5) = (5/7) g sin(theta). Step 2: a = (5/7) x 10 x 0.5 = 3.57 m/s^2.
hint: Rolling needs friction and some energy goes into spin, so it accelerates less than a sliding block.

subject: Physics
question_text: A uniform rod of mass 3 kg and length 2 m has I = (1/12) M L^2 about its centre. Use the parallel axis theorem to find I about one end.
solution_steps: Step 1: I_cm = (1/12)(3)(4) = 1 kg m^2. Step 2: The end is d = 1 m from the centre, so I = I_cm + M d^2 = 1 + 3 x 1 = 4 kg m^2.
hint: Shift the axis by half the length. Add M d squared to the centre value.

subject: Physics
question_text: If g at the Earth's surface is 10 m/s^2, find g at a height equal to the Earth's radius R above the surface.
hint: The distance from the Earth's centre becomes 2R, not R.

subject: Physics
question_text: A planet has a radius 4 times that of the Earth and the same surface g as the Earth. Find its escape velocity (Earth's escape velocity = 11.2 km/s).
solution_steps: Step 1: v_e = sqrt(2gR). Step 2: g is the same and R is 4 times, so v_e becomes sqrt(4) = 2 times larger. Step 3: v_e = 2 x 11.2 = 22.4 km/s.
hint: Escape velocity depends on both g and R: v = sqrt(2gR).

subject: Physics
question_text: One satellite orbits a planet at a radius 4 times the orbital radius of another satellite. Find the ratio of their time periods.
solution_steps: Step 1: Kepler's third law: T^2 is proportional to r^3, so T is proportional to r^(3/2). Step 2: Ratio = 4^(3/2) = 8.
hint: Use Kepler's third law: T^2 is proportional to r^3.

subject: Physics
question_text: At what height above the Earth's surface does the acceleration due to gravity become one quarter of its surface value? (R = 6400 km)
solution_steps: Step 1: g' = g (R/(R + h))^2 = g/4. Step 2: R/(R + h) = 1/2, so R + h = 2R. Step 3: h = R = 6400 km.
hint: Take the square root of 1/4 to find the ratio R/(R + h).

subject: Physics
question_text: At what depth below the Earth's surface is g half of its surface value? (R = 6400 km)
solution_steps: Step 1: Below the surface g' = g (1 - d/R). Step 2: 1 - d/R = 1/2, so d = R/2 = 3200 km.
hint: Inside the Earth g decreases linearly with depth, not as an inverse square.

subject: Physics
question_text: A planet has four times the mass of the Earth and the same radius. Find its escape velocity if the Earth's is 11.2 km/s.
solution_steps: Step 1: v_e = sqrt(2GM/R), so v_e is proportional to sqrt(M) for equal radius. Step 2: v = 11.2 x sqrt(4) = 22.4 km/s.
hint: Escape velocity depends on the square root of the mass for the same radius.

subject: Physics
question_text: A satellite is moved into an orbit with four times the original radius. By what factor does its time period change?
solution_steps: Step 1: T^2 is proportional to r^3. Step 2: T2/T1 = (4)^(3/2) = 8.
hint: Use Kepler's third law with r raised to the power 3/2.

subject: Physics
question_text: Two masses of 2 kg and 3 kg are 1 m apart. Find the gravitational force between them (G = 6.67 x 10^-11 N m^2/kg^2).
hint: Multiply the two masses and divide by the square of the separation.

subject: Physics
question_text: A satellite in a circular orbit has a kinetic energy of 5 x 10^9 J. Find its potential energy and its total energy.
solution_steps: Step 1: For a circular orbit KE = GMm/(2r) and PE = -GMm/r = -2 KE. Step 2: PE = -1 x 10^10 J. Step 3: Total = KE + PE = -5 x 10^9 J.
hint: In a circular orbit the potential energy is minus twice the kinetic energy.
final_answer: PE = -1 x 10^10 J, total = -5 x 10^9 J

subject: Physics
question_text: A body is projected upward from the Earth's surface with half the escape velocity. Find the maximum height reached in terms of the Earth's radius R.
solution_steps: Step 1: Energy: (1/2) v^2 - GM/R = -GM/(R + h) with v^2 = (1/4)(2GM/R) = GM/(2R). Step 2: GM/(4R) - GM/R = -3GM/(4R) = -GM/(R + h). Step 3: R + h = 4R/3, so h = R/3.
hint: Use energy conservation with the exact potential -GM/r, not mgh, since h is not small.

subject: Physics
question_text: How much heat is needed to raise the temperature of 2 kg of water from 20 C to 70 C? (specific heat of water = 4200 J/kg K)
solution_steps: Step 1: Q = m c dT. Step 2: dT = 70 - 20 = 50 K. Step 3: Q = 2 x 4200 x 50 = 420000 J = 420 kJ.
hint: A change of 1 C equals a change of 1 K. Multiply mass, specific heat and the temperature change.

subject: Physics
question_text: A Carnot engine works between 600 K and 300 K. Find its efficiency and the work done when it absorbs 1000 J of heat.
solution_steps: Step 1: Efficiency = 1 - T2/T1 = 1 - 300/600 = 0.5. Step 2: W = efficiency x Q_hot = 0.5 x 1000 = 500 J.
hint: Carnot efficiency depends only on the two temperatures, taken in kelvin.

subject: Physics
question_text: 2 moles of an ideal gas are heated at constant volume from 300 K to 400 K. With Cv = (3/2)R, find the heat supplied (R = 8.3 J/mol K).
solution_steps: Step 1: At constant volume W = 0, so Q = dU = n Cv dT. Step 2: Q = 2 x 1.5 x 8.3 x 100 = 2490 J.
hint: At constant volume no work is done, so all the heat goes into internal energy.

subject: Physics
question_text: A gas occupies 2 L at 27 C. It is heated at constant pressure to 127 C. Find its new volume.
solution_steps: Step 1: Convert to kelvin: T1 = 300 K, T2 = 400 K. Step 2: V1/T1 = V2/T2, so V2 = 2 x 400/300 = 2.67 L.
hint: Gas laws need kelvin, so add 273 to each temperature before dividing.

subject: Physics
question_text: Find the heat needed to melt 0.5 kg of ice at 0 C (latent heat of fusion 336 kJ/kg).
solution_steps: Step 1: Q = m L = 0.5 x 336 = 168 kJ.
hint: During melting the temperature stays constant, so only the latent heat is needed.

subject: Physics
question_text: A gas absorbs 500 J of heat and does 200 J of work on its surroundings. Find the change in its internal energy.
solution_steps: Step 1: dQ = dU + dW. Step 2: dU = 500 - 200 = 300 J.
hint: Heat absorbed is positive and work done by the gas is positive in the first law.

subject: Physics
question_text: How much heat is needed to raise the temperature of 2 mol of a monatomic ideal gas by 10 K at constant volume? (R = 8.31 J/(mol K))
solution_steps: Step 1: Cv = (3/2) R for a monatomic gas. Step 2: Q = n Cv dT = 2 x 1.5 x 8.31 x 10 = 249 J.
hint: At constant volume no work is done, so the heat equals n Cv dT.

subject: Physics
question_text: A heat engine absorbs 800 J from the source and rejects 600 J to the sink in each cycle. Find its efficiency.
solution_steps: Step 1: Work = 800 - 600 = 200 J. Step 2: efficiency = W/Q_hot = 200/800 = 0.25 = 25%.
hint: Work done is the heat absorbed minus the heat rejected.

subject: Physics
question_text: A Carnot engine works between 500 K and 300 K. Find its efficiency and the work it does per 1000 J absorbed.
solution_steps: Step 1: efficiency = 1 - T_cold/T_hot = 1 - 300/500 = 0.4. Step 2: W = 0.4 x 1000 = 400 J.
hint: A Carnot engine's efficiency depends only on the two temperatures, in kelvin.

subject: Physics
question_text: A cycle on the P-V diagram is a rectangle with a pressure difference of 2 x 10^5 Pa and a volume difference of 3 x 10^-3 m^3, traversed clockwise. Find the net work done and the net heat absorbed.
solution_steps: Step 1: Work = enclosed area = 2 x 10^5 x 3 x 10^-3 = 600 J. Step 2: Over a full cycle dU = 0, so net heat absorbed = 600 J.
hint: The area enclosed by a cycle is the net work. Internal energy returns to its starting value.

subject: Physics
question_text: Two point charges of +2 microcoulomb and +3 microcoulomb are 30 cm apart in air. Find the force between them.
hint: Convert microcoulombs to coulombs and centimetres to metres before using Coulomb's law.

subject: Physics
question_text: Find the electric potential at a point 3 m from a +6 nC point charge.
hint: Potential is a scalar, V = kq/r. Convert nC to C (1 nC = 10^-9 C).

subject: Physics
question_text: Two capacitors of 4 microfarad and 12 microfarad are connected in series across a 16 V source. Find the equivalent capacitance and the charge on each capacitor.
solution_steps: Step 1: 1/C = 1/4 + 1/12 = 4/12, so C = 3 microfarad. Step 2: In series the charge is the same on each: Q = C V = 3 x 16 = 48 microcoulomb.
hint: In series the charge on each capacitor is the same and capacitances add as reciprocals.

subject: Physics
question_text: Two point charges of 2 microcoulomb and 3 microcoulomb are 0.3 m apart in air. Find the force between them (k = 9 x 10^9 N m^2/C^2).
hint: Convert microcoulombs to coulombs before substituting.

subject: Physics
question_text: Find the electric field at a distance of 0.3 m from a point charge of 3 nC.
hint: Field of a point charge: k times q over r squared. Convert nC to C.

subject: Physics
question_text: A 2 microfarad and a 4 microfarad capacitor are connected in series. Find the equivalent capacitance.
solution_steps: Step 1: 1/C = 1/2 + 1/4 = 3/4. Step 2: C = 4/3 = 1.33 microfarad.
hint: For series capacitors add the reciprocals, which gives less than the smallest one.

subject: Physics
question_text: An electric dipole of moment 2 x 10^-8 C m is placed at 30 degrees to a uniform field of 10^4 N/C. Find the torque on it.
solution_steps: Step 1: tau = p E sin(theta). Step 2: tau = 2 x 10^-8 x 10^4 x 0.5 = 10^-4 N m.
hint: Torque is p E sin of the angle between the dipole and the field.

subject: Physics
question_text: Find the electric potential at a point 0.9 m from a point charge of 1 microcoulomb.
hint: Potential is a scalar: k q over r with no direction.

subject: Physics
question_text: A conducting sphere of radius 0.1 m carries a charge of 1 nC. Find the potential and the electric field at a point 0.05 m from its centre.
solution_steps: Step 1: The point is inside the conductor, so E = 0. Step 2: The potential inside equals the surface value: V = kQ/R = 9 x 10^9 x 10^-9/0.1 = 90 V.
hint: Inside a conductor the field is zero but the potential is not zero, it is constant.

subject: Physics
question_text: A 10 microfarad capacitor is charged to 100 V. Find the energy stored in it.
hint: Use energy = half C V squared, with C in farads.

subject: Physics
question_text: Resistors of 6 ohm and 3 ohm are connected in parallel across a 12 V battery. Find the equivalent resistance and the total current.
hint: In parallel the same voltage appears across each resistor. Use the reciprocal rule for the equivalent resistance.

subject: Physics
question_text: A cell of emf 12 V and internal resistance 1 ohm is connected to a 5 ohm resistor. Find the current and the terminal voltage.
solution_steps: Step 1: I = E / (R + r) = 12 / 6 = 2 A. Step 2: V = E - I r = 12 - 2 x 1 = 10 V (equal to I R = 2 x 5).
hint: Add the internal resistance to the external resistance for the total resistance in the loop.

subject: Physics
question_text: A 1000 W heater runs for 3 hours every day. Find the energy used in a 30-day month in kWh, and the cost at Rs 7 per unit.
solution_steps: Step 1: Power = 1 kW. Step 2: Energy = 1 x 3 x 30 = 90 kWh. Step 3: Cost = 90 x 7 = Rs 630.
hint: Convert watts to kilowatts, then multiply by the hours used.

subject: Physics
question_text: A copper wire 2 m long has a cross-sectional area of 10^-6 m^2. Find its resistance if rho = 1.7 x 10^-8 ohm m.
solution_steps: Step 1: R = rho L/A. Step 2: R = 1.7 x 10^-8 x 2/10^-6 = 0.034 ohm.
hint: Resistance grows with length and shrinks with area.

subject: Physics
question_text: A 12 V battery is connected across a 4 ohm resistor. Find the current.
solution_steps: Step 1: I = V/R = 12/4 = 3 A.
hint: Ohm's law: current is voltage divided by resistance.

subject: Physics
question_text: Find the equivalent resistance of 6 ohm and 3 ohm resistors connected in parallel.
hint: For two resistors in parallel use product over sum. The result is below 3 ohm.

subject: Physics
question_text: A cell of emf 6 V and internal resistance 0.5 ohm is connected to a 2.5 ohm resistor. Find the current and the terminal voltage.
solution_steps: Step 1: I = E/(R + r) = 6/3 = 2 A. Step 2: V = E - I r = 6 - 1 = 5 V.
hint: The internal resistance is in series with the load. The terminal voltage is less than the emf.

subject: Physics
question_text: A 100 W bulb is used for 5 hours. Find the energy consumed in kWh and in joules.
solution_steps: Step 1: E = P t = 0.1 kW x 5 h = 0.5 kWh. Step 2: 1 kWh = 3.6 x 10^6 J, so E = 1.8 x 10^6 J.
hint: Convert watts to kilowatts before multiplying by hours.

subject: Physics
question_text: In a balanced Wheatstone bridge P = 10 ohm, Q = 20 ohm and R = 15 ohm. Find the unknown resistance S.
solution_steps: Step 1: Balance condition P/Q = R/S. Step 2: S = R Q/P = 15 x 20/10 = 30 ohm.
hint: At balance the ratio of the first pair equals the ratio of the second pair.

subject: Physics
question_text: A battery of emf 10 V and internal resistance 2 ohm is connected to a variable load. Find the load for maximum power and that maximum power.
solution_steps: Step 1: Maximum power transfer when R = r = 2 ohm. Step 2: I = 10/(2 + 2) = 2.5 A. Step 3: P = I^2 R = 6.25 x 2 = 12.5 W.
hint: Power to the load is largest when the load equals the internal resistance.

subject: Physics
question_text: A proton moves at 2 x 10^6 m/s perpendicular to a magnetic field of 0.1 T. Find the force on it (q = 1.6 x 10^-19 C).
solution_steps: Step 1: Perpendicular motion means sin(theta) = 1. Step 2: F = q v B = 1.6 x 10^-19 x 2 x 10^6 x 0.1 = 3.2 x 10^-14 N.
hint: Perpendicular means sin(theta) = 1, so F = q v B.

subject: Physics
question_text: A 0.5 m long wire carrying 4 A is placed perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.2 T. Find the force on the wire.
solution_steps: Step 1: F = B I L sin(theta) with theta = 90 degrees. Step 2: F = 0.2 x 4 x 0.5 = 0.4 N.
hint: Use F = B I L sin(theta) with theta = 90 degrees.

subject: Physics
question_text: A metal rod 0.5 m long moves at 4 m/s perpendicular to a magnetic field of 0.3 T, with the rod perpendicular to its motion. Find the induced emf across its ends.
solution_steps: Step 1: Motional emf = B L v. Step 2: emf = 0.3 x 0.5 x 4 = 0.6 V.
hint: Motional emf equals B L v when the velocity, field and rod are mutually perpendicular.

subject: Physics
question_text: Find the magnetic field at 0.1 m from a long straight wire carrying 5 A.
hint: mu0 over 2 pi simplifies to 2 x 10^-7.

subject: Physics
question_text: A charge of 2 microcoulomb moves at 3 x 10^6 m/s perpendicular to a magnetic field of 0.5 T. Find the force on it.
solution_steps: Step 1: F = q v B sin(90) = 2 x 10^-6 x 3 x 10^6 x 0.5. Step 2: F = 3 N.
hint: At 90 degrees the sine factor is 1.

subject: Physics
question_text: A proton moves at 10^6 m/s perpendicular to a 1 T field. Find the radius of its circular path (m = 1.67 x 10^-27 kg, q = 1.6 x 10^-19 C).
hint: The magnetic force provides the centripetal force: q v B = m v^2/r.

subject: Physics
question_text: A metal rod 0.5 m long moves at 4 m/s perpendicular to a magnetic field of 0.2 T. Find the induced emf across its ends.
solution_steps: Step 1: emf = B L v = 0.2 x 0.5 x 4 = 0.4 V.
hint: Motional emf is the product of field, length and speed when all are mutually perpendicular.

subject: Physics
question_text: The magnetic flux through a single-turn coil changes from 0.04 Wb to 0.01 Wb in 0.1 s. Find the magnitude of the induced emf.
solution_steps: Step 1: change in flux = 0.03 Wb. Step 2: emf = d(phi)/dt = 0.03/0.1 = 0.3 V.
hint: Faraday's law: the emf is the rate of change of flux.

subject: Physics
question_text: Two long parallel wires 0.1 m apart carry 10 A and 20 A in the same direction. Find the force per unit length between them and say whether it is attractive.
solution_steps: Step 1: F/L = mu0 I1 I2/(2 pi d) = 2 x 10^-7 x 10 x 20/0.1. Step 2: F/L = 4 x 10^-4 N/m. Step 3: Same-direction currents attract.
hint: Use mu0 over 2 pi as 2 x 10^-7, and remember that parallel currents attract.

subject: Physics
question_text: A solenoid has 1000 turns per metre and carries 2 A. Find the magnetic field inside it.
solution_steps: Step 1: B = mu0 n I = 4 pi x 10^-7 x 1000 x 2. Step 2: B = 2.51 x 10^-3 T.
hint: Inside a long solenoid the field depends on turns per unit length and the current.

subject: Physics
question_text: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm. Find the image distance and the magnification.
hint: Object distance and focal length of a concave mirror are both negative in this convention.
final_answer: v = -15 cm (real image in front of the mirror), m = -0.5 (inverted, half size)

subject: Physics
question_text: A convex lens of focal length 20 cm forms an image of an object placed 30 cm from the lens. Find the image distance.
hint: The object distance is negative: u = -30 cm. Then 1/v = 1/f + 1/u.
final_answer: v = 60 cm on the other side of the lens

subject: Physics
question_text: Light travels from glass (n = 1.5) into air. Find the critical angle.
solution_steps: Step 1: sin(C) = n2/n1 = 1/1.5 = 0.667. Step 2: C = arcsin(0.667), about 41.8 degrees.
hint: A critical angle exists only when light goes from the denser to the rarer medium: sin(C) = n2/n1.

subject: Physics
question_text: A convex lens has a focal length of 25 cm. Find its power in dioptres.
solution_steps: Step 1: Convert to metres: f = 0.25 m. Step 2: P = 1/f = 4 D.
hint: Power uses focal length in metres.

subject: Physics
question_text: Find the critical angle for light going from glass (n = 1.5) to air.
solution_steps: Step 1: sin(theta_c) = 1/1.5 = 0.667. Step 2: theta_c = 41.8 degrees, about 42 degrees.
hint: At the critical angle the refracted ray grazes the surface at 90 degrees.

subject: Physics
question_text: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm. Find the image distance and magnification.
hint: Use the mirror formula with the sign convention. u and f are negative for a concave mirror.
final_answer: v = -15 cm (real, in front of the mirror), m = -0.5 (inverted, half size)

subject: Physics
question_text: An object is placed 30 cm from a convex lens of focal length 20 cm. Find the image distance and magnification.
hint: Lens formula: 1/v - 1/u = 1/f, with u negative.
final_answer: v = 60 cm (real), m = -2 (inverted, twice the size)

subject: Physics
question_text: A coin lies at the bottom of a pool of water 12 cm deep (n = 4/3). At what depth does it appear to be when viewed from above?
solution_steps: Step 1: apparent depth = real depth/n. Step 2: 12/(4/3) = 9 cm.
hint: The coin looks closer to the surface than it really is.

subject: Physics
question_text: A thin prism has an angle of 4 degrees and refractive index 1.5. Find the angle of deviation.
solution_steps: Step 1: delta = (n - 1) A. Step 2: delta = 0.5 x 4 = 2 degrees.
hint: For a thin prism the deviation is (n - 1) times the prism angle.

subject: Physics
question_text: In Young's double-slit experiment the wavelength is 600 nm, the slit separation is 1 mm and the screen is 2 m away. Find the fringe width.
solution_steps: Step 1: beta = lambda D/d = 600 x 10^-9 x 2/10^-3. Step 2: beta = 1.2 x 10^-3 m = 1.2 mm.
hint: Convert nanometres and millimetres to metres first.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: How many moles and how many molecules are present in 36 g of water? (H = 1, O = 16)
solution_steps: Step 1: Molar mass of H2O = 18 g/mol. Step 2: Moles = 36/18 = 2 mol. Step 3: Molecules = 2 x 6.022 x 10^23 = 1.204 x 10^24.
hint: The molar mass of water is 18 g/mol. Divide the mass by it, then multiply by Avogadro's number.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: In 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O, 4 g of H2 reacts with 16 g of O2. Identify the limiting reagent and the mass of water formed.
solution_steps: Step 1: Moles of H2 = 4/2 = 2 mol; moles of O2 = 16/32 = 0.5 mol. Step 2: 0.5 mol of O2 needs 1 mol of H2, so O2 is limiting. Step 3: Water formed = 2 x 0.5 = 1 mol = 18 g.
hint: Convert both masses to moles and compare them with the 2 : 1 ratio in the balanced equation.
final_answer: O2 is limiting; 18 g of water

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Find the molarity of a solution made by dissolving 4 g of NaOH (molar mass 40 g/mol) in water to make 500 mL of solution.
solution_steps: Step 1: Moles = 4/40 = 0.1 mol. Step 2: Volume = 500 mL = 0.5 L. Step 3: M = 0.1/0.5 = 0.2 M.
hint: Molarity uses litres of solution, so convert 500 mL to 0.5 L.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: How many moles and how many molecules are present in 36 g of water? (M = 18 g/mol, N_A = 6.022 x 10^23)
solution_steps: Step 1: n = 36/18 = 2 mol. Step 2: molecules = 2 x 6.022 x 10^23 = 1.2 x 10^24.
hint: Divide the mass by the molar mass, then multiply the moles by Avogadro's number.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Find the volume at STP occupied by 8 g of oxygen gas (M = 32 g/mol).
hint: Find the moles first. At STP one mole of gas occupies 22.4 L.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: In 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O, 4 g of hydrogen reacts with 64 g of oxygen. Find the limiting reagent and the mass of water formed.
solution_steps: Step 1: n(H2) = 4/2 = 2 mol and n(O2) = 64/32 = 2 mol. Step 2: Divide by coefficients: H2 = 2/2 = 1 and O2 = 2/1 = 2, so H2 is limiting. Step 3: Water formed = 2 mol = 36 g.
hint: Convert both masses to moles, then divide each by its coefficient to compare.
final_answer: H2 is limiting, 36 g of water

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Find the percentage of oxygen by mass in calcium carbonate, CaCO3 (Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16).
hint: Use the total mass of the three oxygen atoms over the molar mass.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: 50 mL of a 2 M solution is diluted with water to 200 mL. Find the new molarity.
hint: The moles of solute stay the same after dilution.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: 5.85 g of NaCl (M = 58.5 g/mol) is dissolved in water to make 500 mL of solution. Find the molarity.
hint: Convert the volume into litres before dividing.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: 10 g of CaCO3 is heated completely: CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2. Find the volume of CO2 at STP and the mass of CaO formed.
solution_steps: Step 1: n(CaCO3) = 10/100 = 0.1 mol. Step 2: CO2 = 0.1 mol x 22.4 = 2.24 L. Step 3: CaO = 0.1 x 56 = 5.6 g.
hint: The mole ratio is 1:1:1, so all three have 0.1 mol.
final_answer: 2.24 L of CO2 and 5.6 g of CaO

subject: Chemistry
question_text: For N2 + 3H2 <-> 2NH3 the equilibrium concentrations are [N2] = 0.5, [H2] = 1 and [NH3] = 2 mol/L. Find Kc.
hint: The powers in Kc come from the coefficients: NH3 is squared and H2 is cubed.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: For N2 + 3H2 <-> 2NH3 (exothermic), what happens to the yield of NH3 when pressure is increased and when temperature is increased?
solution_steps: Step 1: Gas moles go from 4 to 2, so higher pressure shifts the equilibrium forward and the yield increases. Step 2: The reaction is exothermic, so heating shifts it backward and the yield decreases.
hint: Count the gas moles on each side for pressure, and check whether the forward reaction releases or absorbs heat for temperature.
final_answer: Higher pressure increases the yield; higher temperature decreases it

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Find the pH of a 0.001 M HCl solution, and the pH of a 0.01 M NaOH solution at 25 C.
solution_steps: Step 1: HCl is a strong acid: [H+] = 10^-3, so pH = 3. Step 2: NaOH is a strong base: [OH-] = 10^-2, so pOH = 2. Step 3: pH = 14 - 2 = 12.
hint: For a base find pOH first, then use pH = 14 - pOH.
final_answer: pH = 3 for HCl and pH = 12 for NaOH

subject: Chemistry
question_text: For N2 + 3H2 <-> 2NH3 the equilibrium concentrations are [N2] = 0.5 M, [H2] = 1 M and [NH3] = 1 M. Find Kc.
hint: Raise each concentration to the power of its coefficient. Products go on top.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Find the pH and pOH of a 0.01 M HCl solution at 25 C.
solution_steps: Step 1: HCl is a strong acid, so [H+] = 0.01 M. Step 2: pH = -log(10^-2) = 2. Step 3: pOH = 14 - 2 = 12.
hint: A strong acid dissociates completely. Then use pH + pOH = 14.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: For N2O4(g) <-> 2NO2(g) find delta n and write the relation between Kp and Kc.
solution_steps: Step 1: delta n = moles of gaseous products - moles of gaseous reactants = 2 - 1 = 1. Step 2: Kp = Kc (RT)^1.
hint: Count only the gas moles, products minus reactants.
final_answer: delta n = 1 and Kp = Kc RT

subject: Chemistry
question_text: The Ksp of AgCl is 1 x 10^-10 at 25 C. Find its solubility in mol/L in pure water.
solution_steps: Step 1: AgCl <-> Ag+ + Cl-, so Ksp = s^2. Step 2: s = sqrt(10^-10) = 10^-5 mol/L.
hint: For a 1:1 salt both ion concentrations equal the solubility.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: An acetic acid buffer has [CH3COONa] = 0.1 M and [CH3COOH] = 0.01 M with pKa = 4.76. Find its pH.
solution_steps: Step 1: pH = pKa + log([salt]/[acid]). Step 2: pH = 4.76 + log(10) = 5.76.
hint: Use the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation with the salt over the acid.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: One mole of PCl5 is placed in a 1 L vessel and dissociates as PCl5 <-> PCl3 + Cl2. At equilibrium 50% has dissociated. Find Kc.
hint: Build an ICE table with alpha = 0.5 and substitute into Kc.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: For a reaction with K = 2 at some temperature, the reaction quotient is Q = 5. In which direction will the reaction proceed?
solution_steps: Step 1: Compare Q with K: Q = 5 > K = 2. Step 2: Too many products, so the net reaction goes backward (towards reactants).
hint: If Q is larger than K there are too many products and the reaction shifts back.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: A first-order reaction has a rate constant of 0.0693 per minute. Find its half-life.
hint: For a first-order reaction the half-life depends only on k: t(1/2) = 0.693/k.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: For A + B -> products, doubling [A] doubles the rate and doubling [B] quadruples the rate. Find the order in A, the order in B and the overall order.
solution_steps: Step 1: Rate doubles when [A] doubles, so the order in A is 1. Step 2: Rate quadruples when [B] doubles (2^2 = 4), so the order in B is 2. Step 3: Overall order = 1 + 2 = 3.
hint: If doubling the concentration multiplies the rate by 2^n, the order is n.
final_answer: Order in A = 1, in B = 2, overall = 3

subject: Chemistry
question_text: A first-order reaction is 75 percent complete in 40 minutes. Find its half-life.
solution_steps: Step 1: 75 percent complete leaves 25 percent of the reactant. Step 2: 100 -> 50 -> 25 percent takes two half-lives. Step 3: 2 x t(1/2) = 40 min, so t(1/2) = 20 min.
hint: 75 percent complete means 25 percent remains, which is two half-lives.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: A first-order reaction has a half-life of 20 minutes. Find its rate constant.
hint: For first-order reactions k is inversely proportional to the half-life.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Give the unit of the rate constant for a second-order reaction.
solution_steps: Step 1: Units of k = (mol/L)^(1-n) s^-1 with n = 2. Step 2: This gives (mol/L)^-1 s^-1 = L mol^-1 s^-1.
hint: Rate has units mol L^-1 s^-1. Divide by concentration squared.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: A first-order reaction has k = 0.0693 min^-1. How long will it take for the concentration to fall to 25% of its initial value?
solution_steps: Step 1: t(1/2) = 0.693/0.0693 = 10 min. Step 2: 25% remaining means two half-lives: 100 to 50 to 25. Step 3: t = 20 min.
hint: Count how many half-lives it takes to get down to a quarter.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Doubling [A] doubles the rate of a reaction, and doubling [B] makes the rate four times as large. Write the rate law and the overall order.
solution_steps: Step 1: Order in A: 2^m = 2, so m = 1. Step 2: Order in B: 2^n = 4, so n = 2. Step 3: rate = k [A][B]^2 with overall order 3.
hint: Compare how each concentration change multiplies the rate.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: A zero-order reaction has [A]0 = 0.5 M and k = 0.05 M/min. Find the time for complete reaction and the half-life.
solution_steps: Step 1: Time to finish = [A]0/k = 0.5/0.05 = 10 min. Step 2: t(1/2) = [A]0/(2k) = 5 min.
hint: A zero-order half-life depends on the initial concentration.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Using the Arrhenius equation find by what factor the rate constant increases when the temperature rises from 300 K to 310 K for Ea = 50 kJ/mol. (R = 8.314 J/(mol K))
hint: Put Ea in joules and use the reciprocal temperature difference.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: A reaction has the mechanism: Step 1 (slow) A + B -> C; Step 2 (fast) C + A -> D. Write the rate law.
solution_steps: Step 1: The rate is controlled by the slowest step. Step 2: The slow step is bimolecular in A and B, so rate = k [A][B].
hint: Only the rate-determining step appears in the rate law.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Given E0(Zn2+/Zn) = -0.76 V and E0(Cu2+/Cu) = +0.34 V, find the standard emf of the Zn-Cu cell.
solution_steps: Step 1: Copper has the higher reduction potential, so it is the cathode and zinc is the anode. Step 2: E_cell = E_cathode - E_anode = 0.34 - (-0.76) = 1.10 V.
hint: Subtract the anode potential from the cathode potential, and watch the negative sign.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: How much copper (molar mass 63.5 g/mol) is deposited when 2 A flows for 965 s through a CuSO4 solution? (F = 96500 C/mol)
solution_steps: Step 1: Q = I t = 2 x 965 = 1930 C. Step 2: Moles of electrons = 1930 / 96500 = 0.02 mol. Step 3: Cu2+ + 2e- gives Cu, so moles of Cu = 0.01 mol and mass = 0.01 x 63.5 = 0.635 g.
hint: Find the charge first, then the moles of electrons, then use the 2 electrons per Cu atom.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: A cell has E0 = 1.10 V for a reaction with n = 2 electrons. Find delta G0 (F = 96500 C/mol).
solution_steps: Step 1: delta G0 = -n F E0. Step 2: delta G0 = -2 x 96500 x 1.10 = -212300 J/mol. Step 3: This is -212.3 kJ/mol, so the reaction is spontaneous.
hint: Do not drop the negative sign: delta G = -n F E.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Find the standard cell potential of the Daniell cell given E0(Zn2+/Zn) = -0.76 V and E0(Cu2+/Cu) = +0.34 V.
solution_steps: Step 1: Copper has the higher reduction potential, so it is the cathode. Step 2: E0cell = E0(cathode) - E0(anode) = 0.34 - (-0.76) = 1.10 V.
hint: Cathode minus anode, using reduction potentials for both.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: A current of 2 A is passed through copper sulphate solution for 965 s. Find the mass of copper deposited (Cu = 63.5, F = 96500 C/mol).
solution_steps: Step 1: Q = I t = 2 x 965 = 1930 C. Step 2: Moles of electrons = 1930/96500 = 0.02 mol. Step 3: Cu2+ + 2e- -> Cu, so moles of Cu = 0.01 mol, giving 0.635 g.
hint: Convert charge to moles of electrons, then use the 2 electrons per Cu atom.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Find delta G0 for the Daniell cell reaction with n = 2 and E0cell = 1.10 V (F = 96500 C/mol).
solution_steps: Step 1: delta G0 = -n F E0cell. Step 2: = -2 x 96500 x 1.10 = -212300 J = -212.3 kJ.
hint: A positive cell potential gives a negative Gibbs energy.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Find E for Zn | Zn2+(0.01 M) || Cu2+(1 M) | Cu at 298 K, given E0cell = 1.10 V.
hint: Use the Nernst equation with n = 2 and log of the reaction quotient.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Given limiting molar conductivities (S cm^2 mol^-1): CH3COONa = 91, HCl = 426, NaCl = 126, find the value for acetic acid.
solution_steps: Step 1: Kohlrausch: L(CH3COOH) = L(CH3COONa) + L(HCl) - L(NaCl). Step 2: = 91 + 426 - 126 = 391 S cm^2 mol^-1.
hint: Combine the ionic contributions so that the Na+ and Cl- cancel.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: The conductivity of a 0.1 M solution is 0.01 S/cm. Find its molar conductivity.
solution_steps: Step 1: Molar conductivity = kappa x 1000/M. Step 2: = 0.01 x 1000/0.1 = 100 S cm^2 mol^-1.
hint: The factor of 1000 converts litres to cm^3.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: The same charge passes through AgNO3 and CuSO4 solutions in series, depositing 1.08 g of silver (Ag = 108, Cu = 63.5). Find the mass of copper deposited.
solution_steps: Step 1: Moles of Ag = 1.08/108 = 0.01 mol, so 0.01 mol of electrons. Step 2: Cu needs 2 electrons per atom, so moles of Cu = 0.005. Step 3: Mass = 0.005 x 63.5 = 0.3175 g.
hint: The same number of electrons passes through both cells. Copper needs two per atom.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Predict the shape and the bond angle of the water molecule (H2O) using VSEPR theory.
solution_steps: Step 1: Oxygen has 2 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs, 4 electron pairs in total. Step 2: The pairs point to a tetrahedron, but only the atoms are seen, so the shape is bent. Step 3: Lone pairs squeeze the angle to about 104.5 degrees.
hint: Count the lone pairs as well as the bonds before naming the shape.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Find the hybridisation of the central atom in CH4, NH3 and BF3.
solution_steps: Step 1: CH4 has 4 sigma bonds and no lone pair, so sp3. Step 2: NH3 has 3 sigma bonds and 1 lone pair, so sp3. Step 3: BF3 has 3 sigma bonds and no lone pair, so sp2.
hint: Count sigma bonds plus lone pairs on the central atom: 4 means sp3, 3 means sp2, 2 means sp.
final_answer: CH4: sp3, NH3: sp3, BF3: sp2

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Calculate the bond order of N2 and O2 using molecular orbital theory (N2: 10 bonding and 4 antibonding electrons; O2: 10 bonding and 6 antibonding electrons).
solution_steps: Step 1: Bond order = (Nb - Na)/2. Step 2: N2 = (10 - 4)/2 = 3. Step 3: O2 = (10 - 6)/2 = 2.
hint: Use bond order = (bonding - antibonding)/2 for each molecule.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: State the hybridisation, shape and bond angle of methane, CH4.
solution_steps: Step 1: Carbon forms four sigma bonds and has no lone pair. Step 2: Four electron pairs give sp3 hybridisation, a tetrahedral shape and a bond angle of 109.5 degrees.
hint: Count the electron pairs around the central atom.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Is CO2 a polar molecule? Give the reason.
solution_steps: Step 1: Each C=O bond is polar. Step 2: CO2 is linear and symmetrical, so the two bond dipoles cancel and the net dipole moment is zero.
hint: A polar bond does not always give a polar molecule. Think about the shape.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Find the bond order of O2 and say whether it is paramagnetic or diamagnetic.
solution_steps: Step 1: O2 has 10 bonding and 6 antibonding electrons. Step 2: Bond order = (10 - 6)/2 = 2. Step 3: Two unpaired electrons in the pi* orbitals make it paramagnetic.
hint: Bond order is half the difference of bonding and antibonding electrons.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Describe the shape of NH3 and the approximate bond angle.
solution_steps: Step 1: Nitrogen has 3 bond pairs and 1 lone pair, so 4 electron pairs and sp3 hybridisation. Step 2: The lone pair pushes the bonds closer, giving a trigonal pyramidal shape with an angle of about 107 degrees.
hint: The lone pair takes up a position but is not part of the shape name.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Which has the higher boiling point, o-nitrophenol or p-nitrophenol? Give the reason.
solution_steps: Step 1: o-Nitrophenol has intramolecular hydrogen bonding, so molecules are not linked to each other. Step 2: p-Nitrophenol has intermolecular hydrogen bonding, which links molecules together. Step 3: So p-nitrophenol boils higher.
hint: Hydrogen bonds between molecules raise the boiling point more than those within one molecule.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Find the hybridisation of sulphur in SF6 and the shape of the molecule.
solution_steps: Step 1: Sulphur forms 6 sigma bonds with no lone pair. Step 2: Six electron pairs mean sp3d2 hybridisation and an octahedral shape.
hint: Six bonding pairs around the centre need s, p and d orbitals.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Calculate the formal charge on nitrogen in the ammonium ion NH4+.
solution_steps: Step 1: Nitrogen has 5 valence electrons, 0 non-bonding electrons and 8 bonding electrons. Step 2: FC = 5 - 0 - 8/2 = +1.
hint: Formal charge is valence electrons minus lone-pair electrons minus half the bonding electrons.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Arrange Na, Mg, Al and Cl in increasing order of atomic radius.
solution_steps: Step 1: All four are in period 3, so the radius decreases from left to right as nuclear charge increases. Step 2: The order from largest to smallest is Na > Mg > Al > Cl.
hint: Across a period the radius shrinks because the nuclear charge increases with the same number of shells.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Why is the first ionisation energy of nitrogen higher than that of oxygen?
solution_steps: Step 1: Nitrogen is 2s2 2p3, a half-filled and extra-stable p subshell. Step 2: Oxygen is 2p4, where one orbital holds a pair and the repulsion makes that electron easier to remove.
hint: Compare the electron configurations of both atoms. One of them is half-filled.
final_answer: N has a stable half-filled 2p3 configuration; O loses an electron more easily due to pairing repulsion

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Arrange the isoelectronic ions O2-, F-, Na+ and Mg2+ in increasing order of ionic radius.
solution_steps: Step 1: All four have 10 electrons. Step 2: More protons pull the same electrons closer, so the radius falls as nuclear charge rises. Step 3: Mg2+ (12 protons) < Na+ (11) < F- (9) < O2- (8).
hint: For isoelectronic ions, compare the number of protons. More protons means a smaller ion.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Which has the larger atomic radius, sodium or magnesium? Give the reason.
solution_steps: Step 1: Both are in period 3. Step 2: Across a period nuclear charge increases and radius decreases, so Na is larger than Mg.
hint: Across a period the nucleus pulls the electrons in more strongly.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Arrange O2-, F-, Na+ and Mg2+ in decreasing order of ionic radius.
solution_steps: Step 1: All have 10 electrons (isoelectronic). Step 2: More protons pull the electrons in more, so size falls as nuclear charge rises: O2- > F- > Na+ > Mg2+.
hint: For isoelectronic ions, compare the nuclear charge.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Which has the higher first ionisation energy, nitrogen or oxygen? Explain.
solution_steps: Step 1: Nitrogen has the half-filled 2p3 configuration, which is extra stable. Step 2: Removing an electron from oxygen (2p4) relieves repulsion in a paired orbital. Step 3: So N is higher than O.
hint: Do not rely on the general trend. Look at subshell stability.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Which element has the more negative electron gain enthalpy, fluorine or chlorine?
solution_steps: Step 1: Fluorine is very small, so the added electron feels strong repulsion from the crowded 2p electrons. Step 2: Chlorine has a larger 3p subshell and releases more energy.
hint: Size can work against fluorine here.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Which of Li, C, N and F has the highest electronegativity?
solution_steps: Step 1: Electronegativity rises across a period and falls down a group. Step 2: Fluorine is the top right of these and is the most electronegative element in the table.
hint: Electronegativity increases across a period.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Arrange Be, B and C in increasing order of first ionisation energy.
solution_steps: Step 1: Boron has an electron in a higher-energy 2p orbital, so B is lower than Be. Step 2: Carbon has higher nuclear charge so C is higher than Be. Step 3: B < Be < C.
hint: Be has a filled 2s subshell, which breaks the smooth trend.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Classify the oxides Na2O, Al2O3 and SO3 as basic, acidic or amphoteric.
solution_steps: Step 1: Na2O is the oxide of a strongly metallic element, so it is basic. Step 2: Al2O3 reacts with both acids and bases, so it is amphoteric. Step 3: SO3 is the oxide of a non-metal, so it is acidic.
hint: Oxides change from basic to acidic across a period.
final_answer: Na2O basic, Al2O3 amphoteric, SO3 acidic

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Find the oxidation state and the coordination number of the metal in [Co(NH3)6]Cl3.
solution_steps: Step 1: The complex ion is [Co(NH3)6]3+ because three Cl- balance it. Step 2: NH3 is neutral, so the oxidation state of Co is +3. Step 3: Six NH3 ligands are attached, so the coordination number is 6.
hint: The ions outside the square bracket give the charge of the complex ion.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Write the IUPAC name of K3[Fe(CN)6].
solution_steps: Step 1: The complex ion [Fe(CN)6]3- has six cyanido ligands. Step 2: 3(+1) + x + 6(-1) = 0 gives x = +3 for iron. Step 3: An anionic complex uses -ate, so iron becomes ferrate.
hint: It is an anionic complex, so the metal name ends in -ate. Get the oxidation state from the charges.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Find the spin-only magnetic moment of [Fe(H2O)6]2+, a high-spin d6 octahedral complex.
solution_steps: Step 1: High-spin d6 fills t2g^4 eg^2, which leaves 4 unpaired electrons. Step 2: mu = sqrt(n(n+2)) = sqrt(4 x 6) = sqrt(24). Step 3: mu is about 4.9 BM.
hint: Count the unpaired electrons in the high-spin d6 arrangement, then use sqrt(n(n+2)).

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Find the oxidation state of cobalt in [Co(NH3)6]Cl3.
solution_steps: Step 1: The three chloride ions are outside the sphere, so the complex ion is [Co(NH3)6]3+. Step 2: NH3 is neutral, so cobalt is +3.
hint: Ammonia is neutral, so the metal carries the whole charge of the complex ion.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Find the coordination number of platinum in [Pt(en)2Cl2]2+. (en = ethylenediamine, bidentate)
solution_steps: Step 1: Two en ligands each donate 2 atoms, giving 4 donor atoms. Step 2: Two chloride ligands add 2 more. Step 3: Total = 6.
hint: A bidentate ligand counts twice.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Write the IUPAC name of [Cu(NH3)4]SO4.
solution_steps: Step 1: Four NH3 ligands are named tetraammine. Step 2: Copper is +2 here. Step 3: The name is tetraamminecopper(II) sulfate.
hint: Ligands come first in alphabetical order, then the metal with its oxidation state.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Find the spin-only magnetic moment of the Cr3+ ion (Z = 24).
solution_steps: Step 1: Cr3+ has the configuration 3d3, so n = 3 unpaired electrons. Step 2: mu = sqrt(3 x 5) = sqrt(15) = 3.87 BM.
hint: Count unpaired electrons, then use the square root formula.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: [Fe(CN)6]4- is a low-spin octahedral complex of Fe2+. Give its electronic configuration and magnetic nature.
solution_steps: Step 1: Fe2+ is d6 and CN- is a strong field ligand. Step 2: All six electrons pair up in the lower t2g orbitals: t2g6 eg0. Step 3: No unpaired electrons, so it is diamagnetic.
hint: Strong field ligands pair the electrons before filling the upper level.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: How many geometrical isomers are possible for an octahedral complex of the type [Ma3b3]?
solution_steps: Step 1: The three identical ligands can sit on one face (facial) or in a line round the metal (meridional). Step 2: These are the only two arrangements.
hint: Place the three a ligands first. They can be adjacent on a face or in a plane through the metal.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Is [Zn(H2O)6]2+ expected to be coloured? Explain.
solution_steps: Step 1: Zn2+ has a 3d10 configuration. Step 2: With a full d subshell no d-d transition is possible. Step 3: So the complex is colourless.
hint: Colour needs an empty or partly filled d orbital to move an electron into.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: What is the major product when propene reacts with HBr?
solution_steps: Step 1: Propene is CH3-CH=CH2 and HBr adds across the double bond. Step 2: By Markovnikov's rule H goes to the carbon with more hydrogens (the CH2 end). Step 3: Br attaches to the middle carbon.
hint: Hydrogen goes to the carbon that already has more hydrogens.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: How many moles of O2 are needed to burn 1 mole of ethane (C2H6) completely?
solution_steps: Step 1: For CxHy, O2 needed = x + y/4. Step 2: Ethane has x = 2 and y = 6, so O2 = 2 + 6/4 = 3.5 mol. Step 3: Check: C2H6 + 3.5 O2 -> 2CO2 + 3H2O.
hint: Use x + y/4 for CxHy, or balance carbon, then hydrogen, then oxygen.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Is cyclobutadiene (C4H4) aromatic? Apply Huckel's rule.
solution_steps: Step 1: Cyclobutadiene has 4 pi electrons. Step 2: Huckel's rule needs 4n + 2 pi electrons, which gives 2, 6, 10. Step 3: 4 = 4n with n = 1, so it is antiaromatic and unstable.
hint: Count the pi electrons and compare with 4n + 2.
final_answer: No, it is antiaromatic (4 pi electrons)

subject: Chemistry
question_text: How many moles of oxygen are needed to burn one mole of propane, C3H8, completely? Write the products.
solution_steps: Step 1: O2 needed = x + y/4 = 3 + 8/4 = 5 mol. Step 2: C3H8 + 5O2 -> 3CO2 + 4H2O.
hint: Use x + y/4 for CxHy.
final_answer: 5 mol O2, giving 3 CO2 and 4 H2O

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Give the IUPAC name of CH3-CH(CH3)-CH2-CH3.
solution_steps: Step 1: The longest chain has 4 carbons, so butane. Step 2: A methyl branch is on carbon 2.
hint: Find the longest chain, then number from the end nearest the branch.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Name the major product when propene reacts with HBr in the absence of peroxide.
solution_steps: Step 1: Markovnikov's rule: H adds to the carbon with more hydrogens (the CH2 end). Step 2: Br goes to the middle carbon, which holds the more stable secondary carbocation.
hint: The hydrogen goes to the carbon with more hydrogens already.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Name the major product when propene reacts with HBr in the presence of a peroxide.
solution_steps: Step 1: With peroxide the reaction follows a free-radical path. Step 2: Br adds first to the less substituted carbon, so the product is the anti-Markovnikov one.
hint: Peroxide reverses the orientation of HBr addition only.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: How can ethyne be distinguished from ethene in the laboratory?
solution_steps: Step 1: Ethyne is a terminal alkyne with an acidic hydrogen. Step 2: It gives a white precipitate with ammoniacal silver nitrate (Tollens' reagent), whereas ethene gives no precipitate.
hint: Look for the acidic hydrogen on a triple-bonded carbon.
final_answer: Ethyne gives a white silver acetylide precipitate; ethene does not

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Does benzene satisfy Huckel's rule? Is cyclobutadiene aromatic?
solution_steps: Step 1: Huckel's rule needs 4n + 2 pi electrons in a planar ring. Step 2: Benzene has 6 pi electrons (n = 1), so it is aromatic. Step 3: Cyclobutadiene has 4 pi electrons (4n), so it is anti-aromatic.
hint: Count the pi electrons and test 4n + 2.
final_answer: Benzene yes; cyclobutadiene is not aromatic

subject: Chemistry
question_text: What products are formed when propene undergoes ozonolysis followed by reduction with Zn/H2O?
solution_steps: Step 1: CH3-CH=CH2 breaks at the double bond. Step 2: The CH3-CH end becomes CH3CHO and the CH2 end becomes HCHO.
hint: Each carbon of the double bond becomes a carbonyl group.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Arrange these carbocations in increasing order of stability: methyl, ethyl (primary), isopropyl (secondary) and tert-butyl (tertiary).
solution_steps: Step 1: Alkyl groups stabilise a carbocation through +I and hyperconjugation. Step 2: More alkyl groups on the charged carbon means more stability.
hint: Count the alkyl groups attached to the positive carbon.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Which is the stronger acid, CH3COOH or ClCH2COOH? Explain.
solution_steps: Step 1: Chlorine is electron-withdrawing (-I effect). Step 2: It disperses the negative charge on the conjugate base ClCH2COO-, making it more stable. Step 3: A more stable conjugate base means a stronger acid.
hint: Compare the stability of the two conjugate bases.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: How many stereoisomers can a molecule with 3 different chiral centres have (no internal symmetry)?
solution_steps: Step 1: Each chiral centre can have two configurations (R or S). Step 2: Total stereoisomers = 2^n = 2^3 = 8.
hint: Use 2^n for n independent chiral centres.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Which carbocation is more stable, (CH3)3C+ or CH3CH2+? Give the reason.
solution_steps: Step 1: (CH3)3C+ is tertiary and has 9 alpha C-H bonds. Step 2: CH3CH2+ is primary with 2 alpha C-H bonds. Step 3: More hyperconjugation and the +I effect of the methyl groups stabilise the tertiary ion.
hint: Tertiary carbocations have more alkyl groups donating electrons.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: How many stereoisomers are possible for a molecule with 2 different chiral centres?
solution_steps: Step 1: Number of stereoisomers = 2^n with n = 2. Step 2: 2^2 = 4.
hint: Each different chiral centre doubles the count.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Which is a stronger acid, CH3COOH or ClCH2COOH? Give the reason.
solution_steps: Step 1: Chlorine is electron-withdrawing (-I effect). Step 2: It stabilises the carboxylate ion, so ClCH2COO- is a more stable conjugate base. Step 3: A more stable conjugate base means a stronger acid.
hint: A more stable conjugate base gives a stronger acid.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: State the directing effect of the -OH group on a benzene ring and whether it activates or deactivates the ring.
solution_steps: Step 1: The oxygen lone pair is donated into the ring by the +M effect. Step 2: This raises electron density at the ortho and para positions, so the ring is activated.
hint: Electron-donating groups push the electron density into the ring.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Predict the mechanism when tert-butyl bromide is treated with aqueous KOH.
solution_steps: Step 1: The tertiary carbon is hindered and forms a stable carbocation. Step 2: The slow step is ionisation of the C-Br bond, followed by attack of the nucleophile. Step 3: So the reaction is SN1.
hint: Tertiary halides go through carbocations.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Why is phenol more acidic than ethanol?
solution_steps: Step 1: Phenoxide is stabilised by resonance, because the negative charge spreads into the ring. Step 2: Ethoxide has no such delocalisation and is destabilised by the +I effect of the ethyl group. Step 3: A more stable conjugate base means a stronger acid.
hint: Compare the stability of the two conjugate bases.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: How many stereoisomers does tartaric acid, HOOC-CHOH-CHOH-COOH, have?
solution_steps: Step 1: It has two chiral centres, which suggests 2^2 = 4. Step 2: But the two centres are identical, so one form is a meso compound that is achiral. Step 3: The isomers are D, L and meso: 3 in total.
hint: When both chiral centres are identical, check for a plane of symmetry.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Which of these gives a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent: acetaldehyde or acetone?
solution_steps: Step 1: Tollens' reagent is a mild oxidising agent. Step 2: Aldehydes are easily oxidised and reduce Ag+ to silver. Step 3: Ketones are not oxidised under these conditions.
hint: Only one of them has an aldehyde hydrogen that can be oxidised.
final_answer: Acetaldehyde gives the silver mirror; acetone does not

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Will benzaldehyde undergo aldol condensation? What happens to it in concentrated NaOH?
solution_steps: Step 1: Aldol condensation needs an alpha hydrogen, and benzaldehyde has none. Step 2: In concentrated base it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction. Step 3: One molecule is oxidised to benzoate and another is reduced to benzyl alcohol.
hint: Check for alpha hydrogens first.
final_answer: No aldol; Cannizzaro gives benzyl alcohol and sodium benzoate

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Name the product when propan-2-ol is oxidised with acidified potassium dichromate.
solution_steps: Step 1: Propan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol. Step 2: Oxidation of a secondary alcohol stops at the ketone stage. Step 3: The product is CH3COCH3.
hint: A secondary alcohol gives a ketone on oxidation.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: What is formed when propan-2-ol is oxidised with acidified potassium dichromate?
solution_steps: Step 1: Propan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol. Step 2: Oxidation of a secondary alcohol stops at the ketone.
hint: Secondary alcohols give ketones.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Which of ethanal and propanone gives a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent?
solution_steps: Step 1: Tollens' reagent is a mild oxidising agent. Step 2: Aldehydes are oxidised to acids and silver is deposited; ketones are not oxidised.
hint: Only aldehydes are easily oxidised.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Will 2-butanone, CH3COCH2CH3, give a positive iodoform test?
solution_steps: Step 1: Check for the CH3-CO- group. Step 2: 2-Butanone has a methyl group on the carbonyl carbon, so it responds and gives a yellow precipitate of CHI3.
hint: The test needs a methyl group attached to the carbonyl carbon.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Arrange HCHO, CH3CHO and CH3COCH3 in decreasing order of reactivity towards nucleophilic addition.
solution_steps: Step 1: Alkyl groups donate electrons and crowd the carbonyl carbon. Step 2: HCHO has none, CH3CHO has one and CH3COCH3 has two.
hint: Fewer alkyl groups mean a more positive carbon and less crowding.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Name the product when propanone is reduced with NaBH4.
solution_steps: Step 1: A ketone is reduced to a secondary alcohol. Step 2: CH3COCH3 becomes CH3CH(OH)CH3.
hint: Ketones give secondary alcohols.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Write the products when benzaldehyde is heated with concentrated NaOH.
solution_steps: Step 1: Benzaldehyde has no alpha hydrogen, so it undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction. Step 2: One molecule is oxidised and one is reduced.
hint: No alpha hydrogen means no aldol, so disproportionation occurs.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Ethanal is treated with dilute NaOH. Name the aldol product and the product formed on heating.
solution_steps: Step 1: Two molecules of CH3CHO combine, with the enolate attacking the carbonyl carbon. Step 2: This gives CH3CH(OH)CH2CHO. Step 3: Heating removes water to give CH3CH=CHCHO.
hint: Ethanal has alpha hydrogens, so it can form an enolate.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Find the nature of the roots of 2x^2 - 4x + 3 = 0.
solution_steps: Step 1: a = 2, b = -4, c = 3. Step 2: D = b^2 - 4ac = 16 - 24 = -8. Step 3: D < 0, so the roots are complex (not real).
hint: Compute the discriminant b^2 - 4ac and check its sign.
final_answer: D = -8, so the roots are complex conjugates

subject: Mathematics
question_text: If p and q are the roots of x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0, find p^2 + q^2.
hint: Use the sum and product of the roots; you do not need the roots themselves.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Find the minimum value of x^2 - 6x + 11 and the value of x at which it occurs.
solution_steps: Step 1: Minimum is at x = -b/(2a) = 6/2 = 3. Step 2: Value = 9 - 18 + 11 = 2.
hint: Complete the square or use x = -b/(2a).

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Solve x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0.
solution_steps: Step 1: Factorise: (x - 2)(x - 3) = 0. Step 2: x = 2 or x = 3.
hint: Look for two numbers with sum 5 and product 6.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Find the sum and the product of the roots of 2x^2 - 8x + 6 = 0.
solution_steps: Step 1: Sum = -b/a = 8/2 = 4. Step 2: Product = c/a = 6/2 = 3.
hint: Use -b/a for the sum and c/a for the product.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: If alpha and beta are the roots of x^2 - 4x + 1 = 0, find alpha^2 + beta^2.
solution_steps: Step 1: alpha + beta = 4 and alpha beta = 1. Step 2: alpha^2 + beta^2 = (alpha + beta)^2 - 2 alpha beta = 16 - 2 = 14.
hint: Write the expression using the sum and product of roots.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: For what values of k does x^2 + kx + 9 = 0 have equal roots?
solution_steps: Step 1: Equal roots need D = 0: k^2 - 36 = 0. Step 2: k = 6 or k = -6.
hint: Set the discriminant to zero and take both square roots.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Find all values of k for which kx^2 + 2x + 1 > 0 for every real x.
solution_steps: Step 1: Need a > 0, so k > 0. Step 2: Need D < 0: 4 - 4k < 0, so k > 1. Step 3: Combining both, k > 1.
hint: A quadratic is always positive when it opens upward and never touches the axis.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Find the minimum value of x^2 - 6x + 11 and where it occurs.
solution_steps: Step 1: Minimum at x = -b/(2a) = 3. Step 2: Value = 9 - 18 + 11 = 2.
hint: For an upward parabola the minimum is at the vertex.

subject: Mathematics
solution_steps: Step 1: Let y = x^2, so y^2 - 5y + 4 = 0 giving y = 1 or y = 4. Step 2: x^2 = 1 gives x = +/-1, and x^2 = 4 gives x = +/-2.
hint: Substitute y = x squared, solve, then take square roots of both answers.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Find the sum of the first 20 terms of the AP 3, 7, 11, ...
hint: Find the first term and the common difference, then use S_n = (n/2)(2a + (n-1)d).

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Find the sum to infinity of the GP 8, 4, 2, 1, ...
solution_steps: Step 1: a = 8 and r = 1/2, and |r| < 1 so the sum exists. Step 2: S = a/(1 - r) = 8/(1/2) = 16.
hint: Check that |r| < 1 first, then use a/(1 - r).

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Find the value of 1^2 + 2^2 + 3^2 + ... + 10^2.
solution_steps: Step 1: The sum of squares = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6. Step 2: With n = 10 this is 10 x 11 x 21 / 6 = 2310/6 = 385.
hint: Use the standard formula for the sum of squares of the first n natural numbers.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Three numbers in AP have sum 21 and product 315. Find them.
solution_steps: Step 1: Take a - d, a, a + d: sum 3a = 21 so a = 7. Step 2: Product 7(49 - d^2) = 315, so 49 - d^2 = 45 and d = +/-2. Step 3: The numbers are 5, 7, 9.
hint: Choosing a - d, a, a + d makes the sum easy.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Find the 10th term and the sum of the first 10 terms of the AP 3, 7, 11, ...
hint: Use a + (n - 1)d for the term and n/2 times (first + last) for the sum.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Find the sum of the infinite series 1 + 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + ...
hint: Check that |r| < 1 before using the infinite sum.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Find the sum of the first 5 terms of the GP 2, 6, 18, ...
hint: For r greater than 1 use a(r^n - 1)/(r - 1).

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Insert 4 arithmetic means between 3 and 18.
solution_steps: Step 1: There are 6 terms in all, so d = (18 - 3)/5 = 3. Step 2: The means are 6, 9, 12, 15.
hint: n means between a and b make n + 2 terms and n + 1 gaps.

subject: Mathematics
solution_steps: Step 1: Write each term as 1/n - 1/(n + 1). Step 2: The sum telescopes to 1 - 1/10 = 9/10.
hint: Split each term into a difference and watch the middle terms cancel.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: The AM of two positive numbers is 10 and their GM is 8. Find the numbers.
solution_steps: Step 1: a + b = 20 and ab = 64. Step 2: They are the roots of x^2 - 20x + 64 = 0, that is (x - 4)(x - 16) = 0.
hint: Form a quadratic from the sum and the product.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: In how many ways can a president and a secretary be chosen from 8 people?
solution_steps: Step 1: The two posts are different, so order matters. Step 2: Number of ways = 8P2 = 8 x 7 = 56.
hint: The two posts are different, so use permutations rather than combinations.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: How many distinct arrangements are there of the letters of the word MISSISSIPPI?
solution_steps: Step 1: There are 11 letters with I repeated 4 times, S 4 times and P 2 times. Step 2: Arrangements = 11! / (4! x 4! x 2!). Step 3: = 39916800 / 1152 = 34650.
hint: Divide 11! by the factorial of the count of each repeated letter.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: A committee of 4 is chosen from 6 men and 4 women with at least 2 women. In how many ways can this be done?
solution_steps: Step 1: Total ways = 10C4 = 210. Step 2: Subtract 0 women: 6C4 = 15, and 1 woman: 4C1 x 6C3 = 80. Step 3: 210 - 15 - 80 = 115.
hint: Count the unwanted cases (0 or 1 woman) and subtract them from the total.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Find the values of 8C3 and 5P2.
hint: Selections divide by r factorial, arrangements do not.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: How many 3-digit numbers can be formed from the digits 1 to 5 if no digit is repeated?
solution_steps: Step 1: The order matters, so use permutations. Step 2: 5P3 = 5 x 4 x 3 = 60.
hint: Choose each place in turn with one fewer digit each time.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: In how many ways can 6 people be seated around a round table?
solution_steps: Step 1: Fix one person to remove the rotations. Step 2: Arrange the other 5: 5! = 120.
hint: On a round table only the relative positions matter.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: In how many ways can 5 boys and 3 girls stand in a row if all the girls must be together?
solution_steps: Step 1: Treat the 3 girls as one block: 6 units give 6! = 720 arrangements. Step 2: The girls can arrange among themselves in 3! = 6 ways. Step 3: Total = 720 x 6 = 4320.
hint: Do not forget to multiply by the internal arrangements of the block.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Find the number of distinct arrangements of the letters of the word LEVEL.
solution_steps: Step 1: There are 5 letters with L repeated twice and E repeated twice. Step 2: 5!/(2! x 2!) = 120/4 = 30.
hint: Divide by the factorial of each repeat count.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: In how many ways can 8 distinct objects be divided into two equal groups of 4?
solution_steps: Step 1: Choose 4 for the first group: 8C4 = 70. Step 2: The two groups are not labelled, so divide by 2!: 70/2 = 35.
hint: Unlabelled equal groups are counted twice if you do not divide.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: A committee of 4 is chosen from 6 men and 4 women. In how many ways can it include at least 2 women?
solution_steps: Step 1: Total = 10C4 = 210. Step 2: No women: 6C4 = 15. One woman: 4 x 6C3 = 80. Step 3: Required = 210 - 15 - 80 = 115.
hint: Use total minus the cases with fewer than 2 women.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Two fair dice are rolled. Find the probability that the sum of the numbers is 7.
solution_steps: Step 1: Total outcomes = 36. Step 2: Favourable outcomes: (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1) = 6. Step 3: P = 6/36 = 1/6.
hint: List the pairs that add to 7 and divide by 36.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: A card is drawn from a standard deck of 52 cards. Are the events 'the card is a king' and 'the card is a heart' independent?
solution_steps: Step 1: P(king) = 4/52 = 1/13 and P(heart) = 13/52 = 1/4. Step 2: P(king of hearts) = 1/52. Step 3: P(king) x P(heart) = 1/52, which equals the joint probability.
hint: Check whether P(A and B) equals P(A) x P(B).

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Bag A has 3 red and 2 blue balls and bag B has 1 red and 4 blue balls. A bag is chosen at random and a ball drawn is red. Find the probability that it came from bag A.
hint: Use Bayes' theorem: find P(red) over both bags first.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Two fair dice are thrown. Find the probability that the sum is 7.
hint: List the pairs that add up to 7.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: If P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4 and P(A and B) = 0.2, find P(A or B).
solution_steps: Step 1: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B). Step 2: 0.5 + 0.4 - 0.2 = 0.7.
hint: Subtract the overlap so it is not counted twice.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: A bag has 5 red and 3 blue balls. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that both are red.
solution_steps: Step 1: Favourable = 5C2 = 10 and total = 8C2 = 28. Step 2: P = 10/28 = 5/14.
hint: Choose 2 reds out of 5 over 2 balls out of 8.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: A fair coin is tossed 4 times. Find the probability of exactly 2 heads.
hint: Choose which 2 of the 4 tosses are heads.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Given P(A and B) = 0.2 and P(B) = 0.5, find P(A given B).
solution_steps: Step 1: P(A|B) = P(A and B)/P(B). Step 2: 0.2/0.5 = 0.4.
hint: Divide the joint probability by the probability of the condition.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Factory A makes 60% of the items with a 2% defect rate, and factory B makes 40% with a 5% defect rate. An item chosen at random is defective. Find the probability that it came from A.
hint: Use Bayes' theorem: the share of defective items that come from A.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: For a binomial distribution with n = 20 and p = 0.3, find the mean and the variance.
solution_steps: Step 1: Mean = np = 20 x 0.3 = 6. Step 2: Variance = npq = 20 x 0.3 x 0.7 = 4.2.
hint: Variance uses q = 1 - p as well.

hint: Find the slope first, then use the point-slope form with either point.
